rationale: Adopt @assistant-ui/react as the single direct dependency, plus @assistant-ui/react-markdown only if formatted assistant output is required. @assistant-ui/core, @assistant-ui/tap and @assistant-ui/store arrive transitively and must be allowlisted because they are required peers, not optional extras; @assistant-ui/store was missing from the original four-package list. All five are MIT, provenance-signed, free of install scripts and advisories, and the repository publishes through OIDC trusted publishing with a protected environment. The residual risks are footprint (63 MB full install, about 135 KB gzip) and 0.x churn (roughly 30 releases per quarter), so pin exact versions, import only from @assistant-ui/react, keep rehype-raw disabled, and re-review on the 90-day cadence.
decided_by: frontend-platform; revalidated by opencode-review (delegated by dbs-amoswong)
criteria: Permissive license across the full dependency tree
No install scripts in the dependency tree
No telemetry or network calls unless explicitly configured

alternatives_considered.name: Import @assistant-ui/react only
alternatives_considered.reason: The only direct application import; it brings core, store and tap as required peers and keeps the public surface small.

alternatives_considered.name: Import @assistant-ui/core directly
alternatives_considered.reason: Core is a transitive runtime beneath react. Importing it directly expands the API surface and bypasses the supported React entry point.

alternatives_considered.name: @assistant-ui/react-markdown
alternatives_considered.reason: Only needed for formatted assistant output; it adds about 87 packages and 72 KB gzip, and raw HTML remains disabled by default.

alternatives_considered.name: Build a custom chat UI
alternatives_considered.reason: The streaming, tool-call, attachment, markdown and accessibility surface is large; no local build spike or cheaper maintained alternative was reviewed.

conditions: Pin @assistant-ui/react 0.15.31, core 0.3.31, store 0.3.22, tap 0.9.24 and react-markdown 0.14.24 exactly.
Import only from @assistant-ui/react; do not import core, store or tap directly.
Allowlist core, store and tap because they are required peers, not optional extras.
Adopt @assistant-ui/react-markdown only if formatted assistant output is required.
Keep rehype-raw disabled; raw HTML must go through the approved sanitizer requirement.
Keep AssistantCloud and telemetry opt-in; do not construct a cloud client unless explicitly configured.
Re-review on the 90-day cadence because the suite is 0.x and ships roughly 30 releases per quarter.
unknowns: No local browser spike was run for assistant-ui; the evidence is static tree, bundle and pipeline measurement.
The 0.x API surface changes frequently; exact pins and deliberate upgrades are required.
assistant-cloud is MIT and opt-in, but using the hosted service would be a separate commercial decision.
The full 183-package install footprint is large even though bundlers discard source and source maps.
The latest patches at audit time were @assistant-ui/react 0.15.32 and @assistant-ui/core 0.3.32; the decision pins the reviewed 0.15.31 and 0.3.31 until a patch re-review.
reversal_cost: Moderate: the chat surface is a bounded UI layer, but replacing it means rebuilding thread, composer and markdown integration.
review_triggers: A package in the suite drops React 18 or 19 support.
A new advisory or install script appears anywhere in the tree.
The OIDC publish pipeline or provenance attestations change.
The suite enables telemetry or a default network call.
A patch release changes peer ranges, telemetry or the install-script tree.
A 1.0 release or a maintained competitor makes the 0.x churn unacceptable.
